briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon/evening. We will now commence the climate briefing for July 29, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Warning: Widespread and Intensifying Extreme Climate Disasters
sections.content: Globally, climate change is intensifying monsoons, leading to extreme rainfall accompanied by casualties [1]. In Europe, widespread wildfires are raging fiercely in areas such as France, Spain, and Ontario, alongside heatwaves and droughts [3, 104, 107, 108, 111, 113, 122, 123]. The UN Climate Change Convention has categorized the European wildfires as climate crisis damage, urging an end to fossil fuel use, and warned that 'the climate alarm is ringing loudly' amidst the ongoing fires [3, 111]. The Korean Peninsula is also facing simultaneous climate disasters, including extreme heatwaves, tropical nights, and severe drought in the southern regions, following the end of the monsoon rains on July 29 [16, 96]. Notably, Busan recorded a new historical high temperature of 38.8 degrees Celsius, and Yangsan in Gyeongnam exceeded 40 degrees Celsius [99], leading to severe casualties and deteriorating working conditions [97, 98, 100, 101].

sections.title: ⚠️ Hidden Threats and Economic Warnings of Climate Change
sections.content: Beyond immediate disasters, climate change is causing hidden problems that threaten the foundations of our lives. Concerns about health and food security are growing, with global sleep deprivation doubling due to climate change [103, 118], and essential nutrients in food decreasing, leading to 'hidden hunger' [106]. Furthermore, warnings have been issued that urban water supply depletion due to climate change could nearly double water utility bills in the United States [117]. Domestically, KAIST has for the first time identified a 'hidden environmental vicious cycle' – accelerated plastic degradation due to heatwaves and microplastic generation by green algae – presenting new environmental threats [7, 21]. These risks are also materializing in financial markets: MSCI warned against climate change, stating, 'Ignore heatwaves, and your accounts will melt' [2], and NH Investment & Securities diagnosed the potential for a surge in defaults by 580 billion won if global warming is left unaddressed [9].

sections.title: 🌱 Carbon Neutrality and Climate Change Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst these crises, various efforts and positive progress continue in response to climate change. Vietnam has strengthened cooperation with APEC on sustainable forest management, emphasizing it as key to climate change response [5]. Domestically, ecosystem adaptation efforts are active, with Daegu Grand Park beginning to create climate-resilient green spaces through trial planting of southern tree species [6, 11, 13]. Gyeonggi Province has taken proactive measures by releasing climate disaster maps that indicate heatwave and flood risks at the alley level [19], while Yongin Special City and Hampyeong County are enhancing agricultural resilience by providing education on climate change-responsive floriculture and cultivation techniques [12, 18]. Businesses and academia are also actively pursuing carbon neutrality: LocknLock released an ESG report detailing a 41% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions [20], and Chung-Ang University is intensifying AI-based carbon neutrality research [23, 34], seeking technological solutions.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Challenges and Tasks in Domestic and International Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is central to addressing climate change, yet it simultaneously presents numerous challenges and tasks. Domestically, there are ongoing threats to the livelihoods of rural and fishing communities due to renewable energy facility installations, and persistent calls for the withdrawal of the setback distance ordinance [63, 65]. Increased solar power generation is also leading to output control of nuclear power plants, adding complexity to grid operation [80]. The case of global company Meta deciding to withdraw from RE100 after 10 years, following its '100% renewable energy' declaration in 2016 [70, 75], demonstrates the difficulty in achieving renewable energy transition goals. Nevertheless, positive developments continue: Hanwha Solutions maintained profitability with a strong performance in its renewable energy sector, recording operating profits in the 300 billion won range in the second quarter [68, 77, 81, 86, 89, 95]. Jeju Province is also accelerating the creation of a 'green energy' ecosystem by integrating AI and renewable energy [78, 85]. Meanwhile, the achievement rate of carbon neutrality plan reduction targets for 226 basic local governments has been found to be low [44], and criticisms have been raised regarding the 'flexibility clause' of the Carbon Neutrality Act [50], indicating a need to enhance the effectiveness of policy implementation.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing once again reminds us that the climate crisis is a present reality, emphasizing the importance of immediate and multifaceted responses. This concludes the climate briefing for July 29, 2026.
